CENTRAL POLICE Station.
3rd November 1919.

REPORT ON Zaahn and Russian Newspaper called Shanghai Life.

Made by D. S. I. Givens. Forwarded by Office of Chief Detective Officer.

Sir,

D. S. I. Givens called at the Netherlands Consulate on
20th September, and asked if Zaahn was a Dutch subject and
whether he was favourably known at the Consulate. The
Acting Consul General replied to both questions in the affir-
mative. Nothing was said which could possibly have caused
the Consul General to write a letter about Zaahn possessing
an unauthorised certificate.

According to the latest issues of Shanghai Life, Zaahn
is still its de jure editor. Inquiries go to show that it
is still printed by the Mercantile Printing Co., No. 26
Weihaiwei Road, and is published at No. 291 Avenue Joffre.

ASH
11/10

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. Givens
D. S. I.

C. D. O.

关于 Zaahn 及俄文报纸《上海生活》（Shanghai Life）的报告。

由 D. S. I. Givens 撰写。经首席侦探官办公室转发。

先生，

D. S. I. Givens 于9月20日拜访荷兰领事馆，询问 Zaahn 是否为荷兰臣民，以及他在领事馆方面是否有良好声誉。代理总领事对这两个问题均给予了肯定答复。并未提及任何可能导致总领事就 Zaahn 持有未经授权的证书一事致函的内容。

根据最新几期《上海生活》报，Zaahn 仍是其法定编辑。调查显示，该报仍由威海卫路26号的商业印刷公司（Mercantile Printing Co.）印刷，并在霞飞路291号出版。

ASH
10月11日

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
J. Givens

Shanghai Municipal Police.

CENTRAL POLICE Station.
7th Oct. 1919.

REPORT ON Editorial Staff of Shanghai Life.

Made by D.S.I.Givens Forwarded by Office of Chief Detective.

Sir,

Enquiries regarding the staff of the Russian paper called Shanghai Life go to show that G.G. Zaahn, No. 291A Avenue Joffre, who accepts the responsibilities connected with the editorship, is a Dutchman. He came to Shanghai in 1915, since when he has been employed with Olivier & Co., No. 16 Museum Road.

G. Semeskov, who is editor in the real sense of the word, is a Russian. He arrived in Shanghai on April 9th 1919. He is said to have gained some notoriety in Vladivostock for extremist ideas, and began to consort with people suspected of Bolshevist sympathies soon after arriving here. Semeshko started a newspaper in Russian called the "Shanghai Chronicle" on June 29th 1919. It published seditious articles in its first issue and was suppressed on July 1st.

The other names given as belonging to the editorial staff are noms de plume of Semeshkov.

The "Shanghai Life" is printed by the Mercantile Printing Co., No. 26 Weihaiwei Road.

I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
J.H. Givens
D.S.I.

C.D.O.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

中央巡捕房。
1919年10月7日。

关于《上海生活》报编辑人员的报告。

由 D.S.I. Givens 撰写，经首席侦探办公室转发。

先生，

关于名为《上海生活》的俄文报纸工作人员的调查显示，居住在霞飞路291A号的 G.G. Zaahn 是一名荷兰人，他承担与编辑工作相关的责任。他于1915年来到上海，此后一直受雇于博物馆路16号的 Olivier & Co. 公司。

G. Semeskov 是真正意义上的编辑，他是俄罗斯人。他于1919年4月9日抵达上海。据说他因极端主义思想在海参崴（Vladivostock）声名狼藉，抵达此处后不久便开始与涉嫌同情布尔什维克的人士交往。Semeshko 于1919年6月29日创办了一份名为《上海纪事》（Shanghai Chronicle）的俄文报纸。该报第一期即刊登煽动性文章，并于7月1日被查禁。

列出的其他属于编辑人员的姓名均为 Semeshkov 的笔名。

《上海生活》报由威海卫路26号的商业印刷公司（Mercantile Printing Co.）印刷。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
J.H. Givens
侦探副督察 (D.S.I.)

Names of the Editorial Staff of the New Russian publication
called "Shanghai Life" and a synopsis of its contents.

September 21st 1919

Shanghai Life.

Editor G. G. Zaahn (Residing at 291 Avenue Joffre)
Editorial staff:- A. N. Baidouyny
M. B. Vyshensky
I. I. Gnnorsky
Gr. F. Semeshko and others.
A Social, Political and Industrial Journal.

The leading article.

It is our hope to create in Shanghai an independent,
progressive Russian gazette. Our task, however, as may be
seen from the fate of the "Shanghai Chronicle", is very
difficult. The worst phase of the predicament in which we find
ourselves is the lack of definite laws and regulations
for our guidance. Our paper will have to submit to the
personal views of narrow administrators who are not equal
to their positions. We cannot help this state of affairs
and must act as newspapermen had to do in the time of the
censorship. We can give a hint of what our thoughts are.
We must state openly to our readers that Russians did
not enjoy liberty of the press, even in Chinese territory,
where other nations can frankly discuss all sorts of questions.
The ever watchful eye of the Russian police penetrates every-
where and Shanghai is no exception. As this "eye" must be
taken into consideration, we are obliged to use the language
of Ysop (fable langauge) in order to preserve our paper.
Our aims, your problems ......... are clear.
We are trying to provide for the Russian emigrants who
are in Shanghai and in China generally a good independent,
progressive, democratic and impartial paper.
We are doing our best, and it is up to the readers, if
they approve of our aim, to support us in our enterprise.
We shall also introduce into our paper an industrial
section for the purpose of fostering commercial relations
between Russia, China and the Dutch Indies.
Reuter's Telegrams.
A report on the suppression of the Shanghai Chronicle,
how the editor was sued in the Russian Consular authorities
and fined Rbls 50. and how the Russian Mission in Peking
nullified the verdict of the Consular Court.
A treatise on the magazine "Life in the East" in which
the editors are compared to the agents of Chinese prostitutes,
who are to be seen nightly on Foochow Road for printing porno-
graphic articles and pictures. [distributing]
Local Russian News.
News from Siberia as reprinted from various Siberian
papers in Russian.
Case in the Russian Consular Court:
Count Lautrec Savine de Toulouse.

1919年9月21日

《上海生活》。

编辑 G. G. Zaahn（居住于霞飞路291号）
编辑人员：- A. N. Baidouyny
M. B. Vyshensky
I. I. Gnnorsky
Gr. F. Semeshko 等人。
一份社会、政治及工业期刊。

社论。

我们希望在上海创办一份独立、进步的俄文报刊。然而，正如从《上海纪事》的命运所看到的那样，我们的任务非常艰巨。我们所处困境中最糟糕的阶段是缺乏明确的法律法规供我们遵循。我们的报纸不得不屈从于那些才不配位的狭隘管理者的个人观点。我们对这种状况无能为力，必须像审查制度时期的报人那样行事。我们可以暗示我们的想法。我们必须向读者公开声明，即使在中国领土上，俄罗斯人也未享有新闻自由，而在该地，其他国家可以坦率地讨论各种问题。俄罗斯警察时刻警惕的目光无处不在，上海也不例外。由于必须考虑到这只“眼睛”，为了保住我们的报纸，我们不得不使用伊索寓言式的语言（fable langauge）。我们的目标，你们的问题……是清楚的。
我们正努力为居住在上海及整个中国的俄罗斯移民提供一份优秀的、独立的、进步的、民主的和公正的报纸。
我们正在尽力而为，如果读者赞同我们的目标，就由他们来支持我们的事业。
我们还将在报纸中增设工业版块，旨在促进俄罗斯、中国与荷属东印度之间的商业关系。
路透社电报。
关于《上海纪事》被查禁的报道，编辑如何被俄罗斯领事当局起诉并罚款50卢布，以及北京俄罗斯公使馆如何撤销了领事法庭的判决。
一篇关于杂志《东方生活》（Life in the East）的论文，其中将编辑比作福州路上每晚可见的中国妓院的拉客者，因为他们印刷色情文章和图片。[分发]

No. 5347.

The undersigned states that this Consulate
General has no objection that Mr Gualtherus H. Zahn,
Netherlands subject, living in Shanghai, starts there
the publication and the printing of a paper in the
Russian language, tending to thwart bolshevism in
Russia and to favour a purely democratic government
as the one represented at the moment by the rule of
Admiral Koltchak and General Denikine. The princi-
pal aim of the said paper will be the development of
the commercial relations between Siberia, China,
the Netherlands and Netherland colonies. The name
of the paper, which has been registered at the
Chancery of the Consulate General, will be "Shanghai
Life" (          ).

Secretary of Legation,
in charge of the Consulate General
(signed) W.J. Quarles Van Ufford.

Shanghai, August 28, 1919

第 5347 号。

签署人声明，本总领事馆不反对荷兰臣民 Gualtherus H. Zahn 先生（居住于上海）在上海创办并印刷一份俄文报纸，该报旨在挫败俄罗斯的布尔什维主义，并支持纯粹的民主政府，即目前由科尔恰克海军上将（Admiral Koltchak）和邓尼金将军（General Denikine）统治所代表的政府。该报的主要宗旨是发展西伯利亚、中国、荷兰及荷兰殖民地之间的商业关系。该报名称已在总领事馆秘书处注册，为《上海生活》（Shanghai Life）（          ）。

公使馆秘书，
兼管总领事馆事务
（签名）W.J. Quarles Van Ufford.
